Nonogram on NoCharge: Clues and Accessibility

Current NoCharge Nonogram offers formula-derived 5×5 and 10×10 patterns, visible run clues, three-state cells, and no saved completion count.

By NoCharge·Reviewed by NoCharge·Published August 22, 2026·Updated November 24, 2026·2 min read

Bottom line: Current NoCharge Nonogram offers a 5×5 or 10×10 grid with row and column run clues. Cells cycle through unknown, filled, and marked empty; only filled cells that disagree with the pattern prevent a solve.

Read the run clues

A clue such as “3 2” means a run of three filled cells, at least one empty cell, then a run of two. The current page displays row and column run clues with the grid. Cell buttons include their row and column clue text in their accessible names.

Mark a cell

Activate a cell to cycle it from unknown to filled, then marked empty, then back to unknown. Marking an empty square is optional. The puzzle completes when every required filled square is marked filled and no non-solution square is marked filled; unmarked empty cells may remain unknown.

Both sizes use the same basic button controls. The 10×10 version also provides row and column selectors and a Mark selected cell button. There is no separate “Show clues as text” mode or Undo control in the current interface.

What the current puzzle set is

The source defines one deterministic pattern for each size using a distance-from-center rule, then derives row and column run clues from that pattern. It is not a 24-puzzle hand-curated library, and the current page does not claim that every clue set was solver-verified for unique solutions.

No timer or saved puzzle count

The game has no countdown or streak. Its board, selected size, and marks remain in page state; reset returns to the starting puzzle. NoCharge V2 does not save a completed-puzzle count or provide a local best record.
